cultural.summary: Pick varieties that cope with downy mildew!
cultural.how: Tyee, Olympia, Melody and Regal are listed as tolerant to downy mildew.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM spinach package (national list; not HP-tested).

cultural.how: Sow on raised beds above 35 cm, in lines 20 cm apart, and thin to 10-12 cm. Water at the roots in the morning and avoid overhead irrigation.

cultural.summary: Be realistic: natural options are limited here!
cultural.how: No natural spray with efficacy data on spinach downy mildew was found. Look for grey-purple mould underneath the leaf with yellow patches on top.
cultural.evidence: Searched NIPHM, UHF Nauni and ICAR sources.

cultural.summary: Round spots with pale centres thrive in humid weather!
cultural.how: Ooty (Sp) 1 is listed as tolerant of Cercospora. Remove infected leaves, thin for airflow and rotate with non-spinach crops.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM spinach variety table; not HP-tested.

cultural.summary: Be realistic: natural options are limited here!
cultural.how: No natural spray with efficacy data on spinach Cercospora was found.
cultural.evidence: Searched NIPHM, ICAR and UHF Nauni sources.

cultural.summary: The grubs live inside the leaf!
cultural.how: Remove and destroy leaves with winding mines early.

biological.how: Hang 4-5 yellow sticky traps per acre just above the crop.

botanical.summary: A neem spray listed for spinach leaf miner!
botanical.how: Spray NSKE at 4% (40 ml per litre of water), or neem oil at 5 ml per litre with 0.5 ml per litre of sticker, covering both leaf surfaces.
botanical.frequency: At first mines; repeat after 10 days
botanical.evidence: NIPHM spinach package; no efficacy percentage given.

botanical.summary: Cake in the soil deters soil pests!
botanical.how: Apply neem or pongamia cake at 100 kg per acre.

cultural.how: Look for curled, sticky or sooty leaves. Wash colonies off with a firm water spray and conserve ladybirds and lacewings.

biological.how: Release 4,000 green lacewing larvae per acre.
Hang 4-5 yellow sticky traps per acre just above the crop.
